idea-plugin.name: Jenkins Builds
idea-plugin.description:
Jenkins and Jira in one tool window: browse jobs, start and follow builds, let a push start a build, run a command and update Jira issues when it is done.

Jenkins

  • A connection that works with corporate servers: preemptive Basic authentication with a password or an API token, CSRF crumbs, the IDE proxy and the IDE certificate dialog for self-signed certificates. Test Connection reports the HTTP status and the answer of the server
  • Jobs grouped the way Jenkins shows them: views, sections, folders and multibranch projects, with status and last build. Favourite jobs, a group of the jobs that are building now, folders you can hide, and a filter
  • The builds of a job, and for a build: causes, parameters, Git revision and branch, changes, test summary, artifacts with download, and a coloured, searchable console log that follows a running build
  • Build with parameters, including branch selectors (Git Parameter) with a searchable list and favourite branches. Stop, cancel a queued build, rebuild with the same parameters
  • A badge on the tool window button: blue while your build runs, green or red when it finished unseen

Auto build on push

  • Rules "when this branch is pushed, build that job", for pushes from the IDE and from a terminal
  • A command per rule, run at once or after the build: in a new terminal tab (PowerShell, Command Prompt, Git Bash), in a new SSH session of an SSH configuration of the IDE, or in the Run window. The job, the branch and the number, result and address of the build can be used in it
  • After a successful build: comment one or several Jira issues with the link to the build and reassign them

Jira

  • One search field as on the Jira search page: JQL or plain words; it can be locked so its text stays
  • An issue with its description, attachments and comments, each comment in a block of its own; pictures, videos and files are links that download to your Downloads folder
  • Add a comment, reassign, create an issue and choose its assignee. Works with Jira Cloud and Jira Server or Data Center

Passwords and tokens are kept in the IDE password store. Open View | Tool Windows | Jenkins Builds and set up the servers in Settings | Tools | Jenkins Builds (tabs Jenkins and Jira).
